# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Avery Jennings**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone]
[Email]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Regence BlueShield — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-22**
- Member name: Avery Jennings
- Member ID: W675944637
- Reference number: POC-CDC085AB1F-87245
- Denied service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
- Plan: Regence BlueShield (Commercial/ACA), Washington
- Governing policy: **Shoulder Surgeries, Surgery Policy No. 228 (SUR228)**, https://blue.regence.com/trgmedpol/surgery/sur228.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for the rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827) requested by my surgeon, and I am asking Regence BlueShield to reconsider that decision and approve the procedure. The notice dated 2026-08-22 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am writing because the records in my chart do contain the categories of information the plan's own policy asks for, and I am identifying each one below so it can be located and reviewed. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day period stated in the denial notice, which gives a deadline of **2027-02-18**.

## The plan's own policy, and what my records show

The plan's policy, Shoulder Surgeries, Surgery Policy No. 228 (SUR228), states which documents must be submitted:

> "The information below must be submitted for review to determine whether policy criteria are met. If any of these items are not submitted, it could impact our review and decision outcome."

> "• History and physical/chart notes • Non-surgical management provided • Diagnostic imaging reports • Documentation of function-limiting pain"

> "Applicable physical examination findings including but not limited to orthopedic tests performed, pain scale(s), range of motion, and/or loss of strength."

Each of those items exists in my record:

**1. Documentation of function-limiting pain.** The policy states:

> "Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and"

My records document 12 months of progressive pain in the shoulder that is unrelieved by rest. They also document that I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. These are ordinary daily activities, and the loss of them is recorded in my chart.

**2. Non-surgical management.** The policy states:

> "Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated:"

and the options that follow include:

> "a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. C ortisone injection; or"

My record documents supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics for 16 weeks, from 2026-04-06 to 2026-07-27, with 18 visits completed, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note. It also documents NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-27 that gave 3 weeks of partial relief. That is a physical therapy course longer than the three months the policy names, plus both of the additional measures the excerpt lists, and the records show I did not respond adequately to any of them.

**3. Physical examination findings compared with the other side.** The policy states:

> "Individual meets all of the following Criteria (1. and 2.) on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side:"

and:

> "a. Functionally limited active range of motion; or b. Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature; and"

My exam documents range of motion limited by pain, and the chart documents that I cannot raise the arm above shoulder height. If the plan requires the examination to be restated in a specific side-to-side format, I ask that it say so, and my surgeon's office can supply the examination note in whatever form the reviewer needs: [additional exam detail from Dr. Reyes' office, if requested].

**4. Positive orthopedic testing.** The policy states:

> "One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs: a. Drop Arm Test; or b. Painful Arc Test; or c. Jobe or Empty Can Test; or d. External Rotation Lag Sign (Dropping Sign); or e. Internal Rotation Lag Sign; or f. Lift-Off Test; or g. Bear Hug Test; or h. Belly-Press Test (Napoleon); or i. Belly-Off Test; or j. Neer Impingement Test; or k. Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement; or l. Hornblower Test (Patte); and"

My exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side. If the reviewer needs the individual test names identified from that exam, my surgeon's office can provide them: [names of the specific positive orthopedic tests, from Dr. Reyes' exam note].

**5. Advanced imaging that correlates with my symptoms and exam.** The policy states:

> "Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates a partial- thickness rotator cuff tear or a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings."

My MRI of the shoulder dated 2026-06-30 shows a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. A full-thickness supraspinatus tear is the structural finding that matches what my exam and my daily life show: pain with overhead use, inability to raise the arm above shoulder height, and inability to sleep on that side.

The policy also contains a separate pathway that begins:

> "The individual suffers from a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear and has associated function limiting pain; and"

My records describe 12 months of progressive symptoms rather than a single injury event, so I am relying on the criteria above rather than this pathway.

## A note on what I have and have not been given

I want to be straightforward about two things.

First, several of the policy excerpts above end with a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the material available to me. I am not guessing at what those additional conditions say, and I am not stating any time frame, measurement, grade or threshold as the plan's requirement unless it appears in the text quoted above. If the plan applied a specific requirement from a part of the policy I have not seen, I ask that the reconsideration identify that requirement in writing so my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

Second, the denial notice tells me the documentation was incomplete, but it does not tell me which of the required items the plan considered missing. Under the policy's own submission list, quoted above, each category — chart notes, non-surgical management, imaging reports, documentation of function-limiting pain, and examination findings — is present in my record and summarized here with dates. If something specific is still needed, I am glad to obtain it; I simply need to be told what it is.

## What I am requesting

1. That Regence BlueShield overturn the 2026-08-22 denial and authorize rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827, as requested by Dr. Reyes.
2. That the review consider the full records referenced here, including the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-06 to 2026-07-27 and the MRI report dated 2026-06-30.
3. That, if the denial is maintained, the plan identify in writing the exact criterion in Shoulder Surgeries, Surgery Policy No. 228 (SUR228) that it found unmet, and the specific document or finding it considers missing.
4. That this appeal be reviewed by a clinician with relevant orthopedic expertise.

I am also enclosing the Washington member appeal form from the plan's member appeals page at regence.com/member/members/member-appeals, and I am sending this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand the plan also accepts appeals by fax at 1-888-496-1542 per its published appeal form, and that I may call the number on the back of my member ID card with questions.

**Enclosures:** [Washington member appeal form], [copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-22], [office/chart notes from Dr. Reyes], [physical therapy discharge note], [MRI report dated 2026-06-30], [medication and injection records]

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Avery Jennings**
Member ID: W675944637
Reference number: POC-CDC085AB1F-87245
[Signature]
[Date]
